designSummary: Single-arm feasibility study; estimates with confidence intervals compared with pre-set progression criteria; no hypothesis tests.
sampleSize: About 60 young people are expected to be offered peer support over the year. With 60 offers, an uptake of 60 percent is estimated with a 95 percent confidence interval of about 12 percentage points either side, enough to distinguish the green threshold of 60 percent from the red threshold of 40 percent. Six-month retention among about 36 who take up the offer is estimated within about 14 points. These numbers are for estimation, not for testing effects.
primaryAnalysis: Uptake with a Wilson 95 percent confidence interval compared with progression thresholds (green 60 percent or more, amber 40 to 59, red below 40).
secondaryAnalysis: Retention, contacts delivered and questionnaire completion against their thresholds; uptake and retention described for young men, daily cannabis users and people without stable housing; the recovery questionnaire's standard deviation for planning a trial.
missingData: Missing questionnaires are counted as a feasibility outcome and not imputed.
multiplicity: Descriptive estimates against pre-set thresholds only.
software: R for intervals; interview analysis in a qualitative data package.
overfittingGuards: Progression thresholds fixed before the first offer
summary: About 60 offers give uptake within about 12 percentage points, enough to apply the progression criteria.
